title: Recent advances in first-row transition metal clusters for photocatalytic water splitting
claim: Ligand substitution, metal incorporation, and control of titanium-oxo cluster nuclearity are routes to tune cluster electronic structure and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
explanation: The review treats structurally precise titanium-oxo clusters as TiO2 models and describes electron-withdrawing phosphonate ligands and incorporated metal ions as means of changing cluster band gaps and hydrogen-evolution activity.
scope: Titanium-oxo clusters used for photocatalytic hydrogen production.
conditions: Surface sites must permit ligand exchange or metal incorporation for the described band-gap-engineering approach.
caveats: The direction and magnitude of an activity change depend on the particular cluster and modification; the review does not give a universal band-gap–activity relationship.
